task_summary: Refactor `permutations` and `permutations_legacy` in `solution.py` to delegate their shared algorithm to one private helper, preserve compatibility and behavior, and ensure `test_solution.py` contains at least two passing unittest methods exercising the public API.
constraints: Work only in the supplied task workspace; do not access parent repositories or external services.
Use Python 3.11+ and the standard library.
Preserve both public function signatures, return types, error behavior, input immutability, imports, and public names.
Return distinct character permutations in sorted lexicographic order; the empty string has one permutation, the empty string.
Maintain type hints; inputs are at most seven characters; no algorithmic complexity constraint is imposed.

success_criteria.description: Both public functions delegate to one private shared helper, with type hints retained.
The public unittest file contains at least two test methods.
The public unittest suite passes using the requested discovery command.
The tests in `test_solution.py` exercise the public API and cover the stated distinct sorted permutation behavior, including the empty string case.

check.rubric: Read `test_solution.py` and assess whether it contains at least two unittest test methods that call the public `permutations` and/or `permutations_legacy` APIs and assert results covering distinct permutations in sorted lexicographic order and the empty-string case. Evaluate only content visible in workspace files; do not infer test execution outcomes.

assumptions: The named files `solution.py` and `test_solution.py` are relative to the task workspace; they may not exist yet and may be created.
The request does not state the exact signatures or error behavior; those are to be preserved from the supplied implementation when present.
The private helper's name and exact implementation are unspecified; the regex criterion expects a private function definition in `solution.py` after the public function definitions.
`python -m unittest discover -v` is the requested test command and is assumed to discover the public test suite from the workspace root.
